Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: original game source sprite sheet for Rail Link: Collapse. Reference image 1 is ONLY a style reference (chunky visible pixels, dark rusty iron, warm lava orange, hard stepped light); reference image 2 is locomotive identity reference. Original artwork, no copying any external game. Transparent RGBA background, isolated sprites, no scenery, no ground plane, no checkerboard painted into image. Coarse crisp pixel art with square pixel clusters, no blur, no smooth bloom, no text, no labels, no numbers, no grid lines, no watermark. Generous transparent gutters, every sprite fully inside its cell. Camera in front of locomotive looking at its nose, slight elevation; track ahead would extend downward toward viewer. Screen-left and screen-right are literal image directions.
Create exactly TEN isolated sprites in a regular FIVE columns by TWO rows sheet, landscape 1536x1024 if possible. Top row: five on-track pickup objects viewed from front and slightly above, with no track drawn. Bottom row: matching simplified HUD icons in exactly same column order. Column 1 accelerator: sharp double forward chevron turbine/booster, angular silhouette. Column 2 decelerator: broad toothed brake clamp, U shaped silhouette. Column 3 shield: pointed-bottom domed heraldic shield plate. Column 4 ammunition: three upright brass cartridges clipped together, three pronged silhouette. Column 5 fall rescue: round rope rescue ring with large grappling hook hanging through it, clear hole and hook silhouette. Each kind must be distinguishable in monochrome by silhouette, not merely by color. Rusty metal and restrained warm highlights, shield may have muted cyan rim. Top objects more dimensional and large, bottom icons compact and simpler. Exactly 5 objects per row, no extra objects.
